evidence: The hunk shows `seamReads(new Map(owned.map(s => [s.name, s.files])), ...)` and `name = dir === '.' ? ROOT_SCOPE_NAME : dir`, so a directory named `top-level` collides with the root and the Map drops one scope. 30527f5 rewrites seamReads to take the owned array, return `reads` as an array and look up `owned[c.scope].name`, and adds a test with a `top-level/` directory beside the root.
guidance_note: When an original PR turns positional data into a keyed map, key it on the record's identity (index or dir+part), never on a display name that a later stage still has to deduplicate.

evidence: `definers` was built only from `content.symbols.defines`, while `live` adds `changed.get(b).defines`, which includes deleted lines, so `1 / definers.get(s)` is `1/undefined = NaN` and the seam drops out. Instead of the reviewer's `?? 1` guard, the agent counts changed-line definitions as the file's own (`defined` now unions `changed.get(f).defines`), so the definer count is real and not a default. A test asserts weight 1 and weight 2.
guidance_note: When one function's symbol sources (current text and patch lines) feed both a membership test and a divisor, build the divisor from the same union before writing the arithmetic.

evidence: This is the same name-keyed Map collision as F1, raised a second time in the same round. The agent pointed to the index-keyed fix in 30527f5, which removes both the dropped-files problem and the shared reads list.

The original PR changed `partCount` to plain `Math.ceil(groupChurn / SCOPE_CHURN_CAP)` with no upper bound. 30527f5 bounds it by `lanesFree = laneCeiling - (merged.size - 1)`, which is the lane-budget option the reviewer named, threaded through `material.proposal({ ..., laneCeiling })`. The fix did not update the plan.test determinism proof to pass the new input, and F9 found that gap.
guidance_note: When removing a bound from a sizing rule, decide in the same commit what bounds it now, and when adding a new input to a pure producer, grep every test that recomputes that producer's output and pass it the same value.

evidence: The original PR removed the guarantee that every part reads its siblings, so in a language the shapes don't parse, a cut concern's parts got `reads: []`. The agent did not add the reviewer's zero-seam fallback branch: 30527f5 makes sibling files candidates at `coupling > 0 || sibling.has(file)`, which keeps one ranking. Two gaps were left: `focusFor`'s sentence still said 'The change couples these files' (F8), and a new 'as before' header claim was false for cuts of more than two parts (F11).
guidance_note: When widening what a list contains (siblings at coupling zero beside detected seams), check every consumer that renders or explains that list, and test the claim at k>2 before writing 'as before' in a header.

evidence: `USE_CALL = /...([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*[({<]/` matches `i < len` as a use, and the unanchored `[&*]Name` matches `flags&MASK`. 30527f5 drops `<` from USE_CALL, anchors USE_TYPE to a token start, and adds a test that `i < len; a*height; flags&MASK` yields no uses.
guidance_note: Before shipping a regex that recognizes code shapes, run it over a line of ordinary control flow and arithmetic and assert it extracts nothing.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: 30527f5 does not touch src/prompt.js, and `elsewhereSentence` with its unbounded `elsewhere.join(', ')` comes from the original PR. The premise holds: the sentence grows with the number of files outside the scope, while the excluded-paths note in the same file is capped. The agent switched it to the bounded excludedPathList and added a count.
guidance_note: When adding a prompt sentence that interpolates a list of paths, reuse the file's existing bounded-list helper from the start rather than `join`.

evidence: Before 30527f5, `reads` held only detected seams, so 'The change couples these files to yours' was accurate. The F5 fix added siblings at coupling zero to `reads`, and focusFor kept the same sentence, so the worker is told about a coupling nobody detected. The agent now carries coupling to focusFor and renders a separate size-split sentence for sibling reads.
guidance_note: When a fix changes what a value contains, read every place that renders that value into prompt text and check the wording still holds for the new members.

evidence: The F4 fix made `laneCeiling` an input to `partitionByDirectory`, but the plan.test check that 'the recorded plan is the partition the workers ran' still recomputes the partition with no ceiling (default Infinity). It passes only because FILES never reaches the cap. The agent added `{ laneCeiling: 4 }` to both comparisons. The packet shows the test hunk but not passRecording's value of 4, which the agent confirmed.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a parameter to a function a determinism test recomputes, update that test to pass the call site's value in the same commit.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: 30527f5's seams.js diff changes only the USE_* regexes and seamsOf's `defined`. The `/^\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*=[^=]/` definition shape is unchanged from the original PR. The premise holds: that shape matches `  err = doSomething()` in any function body. The agent replaced it with tracking of Go grouped declarations and added negative tests.
guidance_note: For each definition shape added to a heuristic table, write a negative test with the commonest non-definition that matches it (here, an in-body reassignment).

evidence: The F5 fix added a header saying siblings are read 'as before', and its only test was a two-part cut. With up to k parts allowed by F4's lane bound and one shared budget, a tie-break `x.scope - y.scope` at coupling zero starves the later parts. The agent interleaved ties across scopes, rewrote the header to say what cannot be covered and that it is named unread, and added a nine-part test. It kept the lane bound rather than the reviewer's cap, because the ticket rejected the flat-rate read.
guidance_note: When a fix claims to restore an old guarantee, test it at the scale the new rule now allows (many parts), not only at the size of the reviewer's example.

narrative: Round 0 found six real defects in the new seam-based partition: a name-keyed Map collision (raised twice), NaN from deleted definitions, an unbounded part count, lost sibling visibility for cut concerns, and false-positive use shapes. The agent fixed all of them in 30527f5, choosing structural fixes over the reviewer's guards (index keys, unioned definers, siblings as zero-coupling candidates). Three round-1 findings came from those fixes: the focus sentence still claimed coupling for sibling reads (F8), the determinism test did not pass the new laneCeiling (F9), and the 'as before' coverage claim failed past two parts (F11). Round 1 would have run anyway, because F7 and F10 were defects in the original PR that round 0 missed.
guidance_observations: The fix commit widened `reads` to include siblings at coupling zero without re-reading focusFor, the one consumer that explains `reads` to the worker.
New inputs to a pure producer (laneCeiling) were threaded to the call site but not to the test that recomputes the producer to prove determinism.
The agent wrote a guarantee into a header ('as before') that was tested only at k=2, while the same commit made larger k possible.
